summary: Satana ransomware dropper with extensive anti-analysis capabilities. The sample matches the Ransom_Satana_Dropper YARA rule with 3 string signatures, contains anti-debugging (ZwGetContextThread, OutputDebugStringA, NtYieldExecution, 4 TLS callbacks executing before entry point), anti-VM/Qemu detection, a massive encoded payload blob with embedded URLs and IPv6 addresses, a Base64 encoding table, and highly obfuscated control flow (cyclomatic complexity 91 in main function). OpenGL API imports (11 functions) serve as anti-sandbox evasion. The dropper contains obfuscated configuration and C2 infrastructure. Persistence mechanisms: not observed. Exfiltration mechanisms: not observed.
key_evidence: YARA rule 'Ransom_Satana_Dropper' matched with 3 strings at offsets 1264, 1628, 1196 — direct family identification
YARA rule 'anti_dbg' matched with 2 strings at offsets 690 and 9350 — anti-debugging techniques present
YARA rule 'Qemu_Detection' matched at offset 44611 — anti-VM/sandbox evasion
YARA rule 'url' matched at offset 49141 (53 chars) — embedded URL for C2 or ransom payment
YARA rule 'IP' (IPv6) matched at offset 22282 — embedded network indicators
YARA rules 'contains_base64' and 'BASE64_table' matched — encoded payload detected
Ghidra string_refs: 4 TLS callbacks (First_tls, on_tls_callback1, on_tls_callback2, on_tls_callback3) — code executes before entry point, anti-debugging technique
Ghidra imports: ZwGetContextThread from NTDLL.DLL — anti-debugging (checks debug context registers)
Ghidra imports: OutputDebugStringA from KERNEL32.DLL — known anti-debugging technique
Ghidra imports: NtYieldExecution from NTDLL.DLL — anti-debugging/anti-analysis
Ghidra imports: 11 OpenGL functions (glBegin, glClear, glColor3d, glVertex3d, etc.) from OPENGL32.DLL — unusual for non-GUI PE, anti-sandbox technique
Ghidra function_metrics: FUN_00401310 has cyclomatic_complexity=91, block_count=91, instruction_count=486, size=2349 — highly complex obfuscated logic
Ghidra strings: obfuscated string 'qfntvthb' referenced by FUN_00402030 — likely encoded key or config
Ghidra strings: massive encoded blob (thousands of chars, non-ASCII) at address 0x401B00+ — encrypted/obfuscated payload or configuration
Malcat static profile: entropy 135, anomalies count 7, file size 50861 — high entropy consistent with packed/encrypted content
YARA rule 'Safeguard_103_Simonzh' matched at offset 6416 — additional malware family signature
